description: Re-executes a previously recorded session identified by its label, rebuilding it from the saved objective and feeding its stored outputs back in through a fixed-sequence generator. It prints the new outcome and where its record was written, and returns zero only if the new session completed.

Prints the matching records from a recorded session's history, selected by a query expression passed as a command-line argument. Throws if the session label or the expression is missing, if no history exists for that session, or if the query cannot be evaluated; otherwise it prints the selection.

Downloads a web address under a time limit, following redirect hops, turning HTML pages into a plain readable form, passing textual and structured formats through unchanged, and marking other binary formats as not shown. It also keeps a copy of the raw bytes and wraps the download in a re-attempt loop, returning a result for the caller.

Syntax-checks every version-controlled JavaScript source under a repository directory, optionally limited to a list of path prefixes, by running the Node check on each one in parallel. It returns a success flag with a message naming the entries that failed to parse, or a count of the sources that parsed.
Checks whether a given commit identifier exists in the repository by asking the version control tool to resolve it as a commit, and resolves to true or false.

Drives one complete session to its end: it records a start entry, awaits the inner loop, and releases the attached helpers in a cleanup block whether the loop succeeds or not. It then writes a digest, records an end entry carrying the result, and returns that result.

Groups an ordered list of planned steps into consecutive batches that may run concurrently. In sequential mode every step is its own batch; a step flagged as a sync point always stands alone, and otherwise a step joins the current batch until its resource claims overlap what that batch already holds, which opens a new batch.

Pauses for a set number of milliseconds, or until a queued item shows up for a session directory, whichever comes first. It returns at once when the delay is zero or when an item is already queued, and it removes its countdown and listener once it resumes.

Refreshes the reloadable parts of the server: it advances a version counter, rebuilds the public interface from freshly loaded pieces, swaps those pieces into the active tool set, and records the refresh. It returns a success flag with the new version and the names of the refreshed parts, or a failure flag with the problem text.

Creates a new session directory, refusing if it already holds a record file. It writes the guidance text and the saved metadata in structured form into that directory, then returns a writer that appends entries to the record file.

Builds a set of lookup operations over a project directory, optionally confined to a remapped location scheme. The literal-or-regex lookup validates the query, match style, reach, case sensitivity, paging and third-party inclusion, finds the target location inside the project, lists candidate documents through version control or a directory walk, and returns the matches.

Writes a knowledge article after validating every argument: the slug must be short and lowercase, the heading and blurb must each be a single ASCII line, the content must be ASCII, the category must be on an allowed set, every cited reference must exist, and each quoted assertion must appear verbatim in its cited reference. On success it writes the article with a metadata header, updates its table-of-contents line, and appends a dated change journal line; any failed check returns a refusal instead.

Adds a record of a spawned worker to either the machine-wide or the per-project ledger. It checks that the number is a positive integer, stamps the record with the time and the author, makes sure the ledger directory exists, archives the old ledger when it grows large, and appends the line. It returns the stored record, or nothing if the number is invalid or the write fails.

Validates a request to the code insight tool: when the request targets a single item by a label, location or prefix field but gives no operation field, it throws an exception explaining that the request would only return a whole-index overview and telling the caller to add an operation. Otherwise it returns without doing anything.
Returns the location of the development sync timestamp record inside the agent plug data folder.

Rewrites an absolute location inside a request payload into a project-based location with forward slashes, for a fixed set of operations that take project locations. It leaves the payload untouched unless the location is absolute, a project base can be found, and the location lies inside it.
Extracts the location from an item that is either a plain string or an object carrying a location text, returning nothing for any other shape.

Reduces a search match, given as a plain string or an object, to a bare document location by removing any trailing line number and leading dot-slash segments. It returns nothing when the match carries no usable text.

Finds the process number of the machine-wide background service that is currently alive. It checks the service's state record first, then falls back to the holder file, accepting a value only if it is a positive whole number naming a live process, and returns nothing when neither identifies one.

Tracks a freshly launched background helper for a project directory: it remembers the helper's process number and launch time, marks the helper as finished with its final number when it ends or fails, and records it in the process ledger as the project's sweeper. It also writes the number and launch time into the project's guard file, then lets the parent go on without waiting for it.

Loads two lookup tables a single time and reuses that pending or finished load on later calls, then derives the alternate names accepted for a file-read operation and for the code search location and result-count entries from them.

Enriches a serialized health reply: when the given string parses into an object, in either of two notations, it merges bundle drift and source health fields into that object's payload section and writes it back in the same notation. Anything that fails to parse or is not an object is returned as it arrived.

Scans a directory for leftover state files that no longer serve a purpose and returns a list of removal candidates, each with the cause it was flagged for. It skips protected entries and flags reservations held by dead processes, guard files that name a dead process, deliberate-shutdown notes older than a set age whose process is gone, and bare reservations stamped more than a day ago.
Performs a cleanup sweep wrapped in a Windows-only guard, passing along the caller's optional settings and returning whatever the sweep produces.

Asks the background worker for its current state through a supplied send function, waiting no longer than a set time limit. If the answer does not arrive in time it returns a timeout failure; otherwise it converts the answer into a worker result.

Announces a change in the next queued item: when the item's identifier differs from the one remembered last time and a push channel exists, it sends a notice to each subscribed address for the next-item and continuation feeds, then stores the new identifier for the next comparison.

Takes an exclusive guard on a file in the agent-plug data folder by creating it atomically and recording the owner's number and start time. If the file already exists, it clears it once when its owner is gone or its last change is older than a limit, then tries again; it returns the file's location on success or nothing when a living owner still holds it.

Compacts an outgoing answer before it is sent: it removes fields that are always withheld or withheld unless a companion flag is set, trims long lists and row excerpts, drops leftover count lines that restate structured counts, and descends into nested payloads, then records in a compaction note what it removed or trimmed.

Sets up a repeating background schedule that, on every cycle, refreshes a deployed build bundle when it has gone stale, and on every hourly-spaced cycle also starts an optional extra job and records any failure it raises. It fires one round straight away, does not keep the process alive, and returns the schedule handle.

Sweeps stale HTTP listening numbers: for each registered number it reads the recorded running copy and monitor state, and if no live server is recorded, the health check fails, and nothing else holds that number, it deletes that number's state files and logs the freeing. It returns the list of numbers it freed.

Registers handlers for interrupt, terminate, hang-up and break notices from the operating system. On each one it stops the subprocesses it started, releases the agent reservations it holds, records the event with the in-flight request count and both totals, and then terminates itself with a success status.
Maps an input label to its standard spelling by calling a shared normalising helper and returns the result.
